newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska wheat helped by rains late in week.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska wheat helped by rains late in week.

text.p: Dry weather early last week allowed corn, sorghum and soybean planting to advance and late week rains aided winter wheat during the week ended Sunday, according to the state's weekly Agricultural Statistics Service update.
The rain fell from Thursday to Sunday in nearly all areas with heavy amounts in the panhandle.

Winter wheat conditions declined from the previous week to two percent excellent, 29 good, 49 fair, 18 poor and two very poor. As of Sunday, 81 percent of the wheat had jointed versus 87 a year ago and the 96 average.
Fourteen percent of the wheat had headed versus 13 a year ago and the 33 average.
Corn was 98 percent planted and 68 emerged versus 93 and 67 a year ago, respectively, and the 88 and 56 averages. Some replanting was needed in southern areas because of crusted soils and wire worms.
Soybeans were 75 percent planted versus 39 a year ago and the 47 average. Eighteen percent of the crop had emerged versus seven a year ago and the 12 average.
Oats were rated two percent excellent, 52 good, 36 fair and 10 poor.
Alfalfa was rated four percent excellent, 39 good, 39 fair, 12 poor and six very poor. The first cutting was one percent complete.
Topsoil moisture was rated 33 percent adequate, 58 short and nine very short. Subsoil moisture was rated one percent surplus, 76 adequate, 22 short and one very short.
